summary: Subhadradis Diskul (1923-2003) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the École du Louvre (~1948-1951). He served as President of the Siam Society (~1982-1986) and Chairman of The Jim Thompson Foundation (~1987-2003).

Subhash Kak is an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist educated at NIT Srinagar and IIT Delhi. He held positions at Imperial College London (~1975-1976), LSU (~1979-2007) as Delaune Distinguished Professor, and Jawaharlal Nehru University (~2019).

Sudhir Kakar (1938-2024) studied at St. Edward's School, Shimla, working in religious studies and related fields. He was a Lecturer at Harvard (~1967-1971), Professor at IIM Ahmedabad (~1971-1975), and Head of Humanities and Social Sciences at IIT Delhi (~1976-1977).

Sue Hamilton completed her D.Phil at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich (~1990-1994) in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She held a post at King's College London (~1994) and taught Paul Fuller and Tse-fu Kuan.
Suk Fun Ng is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (~2010-2014) supervised by Jing Yin and Y. Karunadasa, and studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.

Sukumar Dutt (1891-1970) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Professor of English Literature at Surendranath College (1916) and undertook postdoctoral studies under Giuseppe Tucci (1953-1954).

Sukumar Sen (1900-1992) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1921-1923). He held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1930-1964) and served as Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (1954-1955).

Sukumari Bhattacharji (1921-2014) was an Indologist educated at the University of Calcutta (~1952-1954) and Jadavpur University (~1960-1964). She held posts at Lady Brabourne College (1945) and taught at Jadavpur University (1957-1986).

Sulak Sivaraksa studied at the University of Wales, Lampeter (~1954-1957) and works in Buddhist and religious studies. He served as editor for the Social Science Association of Thailand (~1963-1969) and as Council member and Honorary Editor for the Siam Society.

Sumanapala Galmangoda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as Senior Professor at the University of Kelaniya and Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Sumathi Ramaswamy studied at the University of Delhi, JNU, and the University of Pennsylvania, specializing in history, archaeology, and Indology. She held positions at the University of Pennsylvania (~1993-1995) and the University of Michigan (~2000-2007).
Sumi Lee specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed an MA at UIUC under Alexander L. Mayer (~2003-2006) and a PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. (~2007-2014).

Sumitra Mangesh Katre (1906-1998) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D at the University of London. He held posts at Sir Parashurambhau College, Deccan College (1942-1971), and the University of Texas at Austin (1971-1976).

Sun-Ah Choi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned a PhD at the University of Chicago (~2005-2012) under doctoral supervisor Juhyung Rhi and studied under Richard Neer, Robert S. Nelson, Jaś Elsner, and Aden Kumler.

Sung Bae Park is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who completed his doctorate under Lewis Lancaster (~1972-1979). He held posts at Dongguk University (~1960-1965) and Stony Brook University (1977), and founded the International Association for Wonhyo Studies.

Sungdoo Ahn specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, earning a PhD at the University of Hamburg (~1993-2001) under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as Director at Geumgang University (~2003-2008) and Professor at Seoul National University (~2008).
Sungtaek Cho is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He taught at Stony Brook University (~1995-2002) and served as Director at Korea University (2002-2003).
Sunhee Kim completed a Doctor of Philosophy in Performance Practice at the University of Exeter under the supervision of Phillip B. Zarrilli (~2008-2013).

Suniti Kumar Chatterji (1890-1977) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Scottish Church College, Calcutta, London, and Paris. He held posts at the University of Calcutta (~1914-1952) and served as National Professor in Humanities (~1965-1977).
Supree Kanjanapisarn is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who completed a PhD at Assumption University under the supervision of Veerachart Nimanong (until 2011).
